questions.q: What is the key difference between monitoring and observability, as this lesson defines them?
options: There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable marketing labels
Monitoring watches known signals against known thresholds; observability is being able to answer questions you never thought to ask, using existing telemetry
Observability only applies to Kubernetes clusters, while monitoring applies to any infrastructure
Monitoring requires traces; observability only requires metrics
questions.explain: Monitoring is watching predefined signals against predefined thresholds. Observability is the broader property of being able to decompose a novel question live, using only the telemetry a system already emits.

questions.q: Why are metrics the cheapest of the three pillars to store at scale?
options: Because they are pre-aggregated numbers — a counter or histogram stays roughly the same size whether it represents ten requests or ten million
Because metrics are only stored for five minutes before being deleted
Because metrics never include labels or dimensions
Because metrics are stored exclusively in log files
questions.explain: Metrics are pre-aggregated, so their storage cost doesn't scale with raw event volume the way logs and traces do — that's exactly what makes them cheap enough to alert and dashboard on.

questions.q: In the lesson's trace example, checkout-service shows a 402ms span. What does drilling into its child spans reveal?
options: Every child span took an equal share of the 402ms
payment-service alone accounted for the full 402ms
inventory-service alone accounted for 380 of the 402ms, making it the real bottleneck
The trace contains no child spans at all
questions.explain: The trace tree shows inventory-service at 380ms dominating checkout-service's total 402ms span — information neither a metrics dashboard nor one service's isolated logs would reveal.

questions.q: On a real incident walk-through, what role do logs play after a metric alert fires and a trace has localized the slow span?
options: Logs replace the need for a trace entirely
Logs are only useful before an alert fires, never after
Logs re-aggregate the metric into a different time window
Logs, filtered to that trace ID, supply the specific detail — the actual exception or slow-query cause — that explains why that span was slow
questions.explain: Metrics find that something is wrong, a trace localizes where in the call chain, and logs filtered to that trace ID explain the specific why — the three pillars chain together across an investigation.

questions.q: What does a span represent within a distributed trace?
options: The entire dashboard showing every service's latency at once
A fixed time window, such as the last 5 minutes, used for alerting
One unit of work within the trace — such as one service call or one database query — with its own start time, duration, and parent span
A duplicate copy of a log line sent to two storage backends
questions.explain: A span is one hop in the trace's call chain, carrying its own timing and a reference to its parent span, which is how the full request timeline reconstructs.
